answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities with decaying work-history trust graphs. Every verified job an identity completes adds reputation edges, forming an atlas of real contributions a jury can inspect. Trust decays without fresh work, so a Sybil swarm cannot bank one good week and coast: ten thousand fake identities each need a continuously maintained work history. Think of reputation as a garden — each identity is an island that must be tended, or its standing withers. The attacker's cost compounds with every fake island, rising until mass fakery costs more than honest work.
